headline: Primary scholarship results to be published today, available via two methods
summary: The Directorate of Primary Education announced that 82,500 students will receive scholarships, with 80% from government primary schools and 20% from private institutions.
details: The results of the 2025 Primary Scholarship Examination are set to be published today, Thursday. The Directorate of Primary Education (DPE) confirmed that all preparations for the announcement are nearing completion.

Primary and Mass Education Minister A N M Ehsanul Hoque Milan will officially declare the results at a press conference at the Secretariat this morning. A total of 82,500 students will be awarded scholarships this year.

Of these, 80% of the scholarships will go to students from government primary schools, while the remaining 20% are allocated for candidates from private or kindergarten schools. Scholarship recipients will receive financial benefits under two categories: 'Talent Pool' and 'General Grade'.

The scholarship examination was held across the country, with exams taking place from April 15-18, 2026, in all districts except the three Chittagong Hill Tracts districts. In Rangamati, Khagrachari, and Bandarban, exams were held from April 17-20.

This year, over 640,000 students participated, including 550,000 from government primary schools and 90,000 from private primary schools. The DPE stated that results can be accessed online and via mobile SMS.
The official online portal for checking results is 'IPEMIS'. Out of the 82,500 scholarships, 66,000 are for government primary school students and 16,500 for private primary school students.

The scholarship ratio is 8:1 for government primary schools (one scholarship per eight students) and 5.5:1 for private schools (one scholarship per 5.5 students). Talent Pool scholarships will be awarded to 33,000 students, while 49,500 will receive General scholarships.

Talent Pool recipients will receive BDT 300 monthly and a BDT 225 annual lump sum. General scholarship recipients will get BDT 225 monthly and a BDT 225 annual lump sum. These financial benefits will be provided for two years after students pass Class Five.

headline: 60 kmph winds: Thunderstorms forecast for 20 districts including Dhaka
summary: Severe thunderstorms and gusty winds are expected to hit multiple regions, prompting weather alerts for residents.
details: Thunderstorms and heavy rainfall are forecast for 20 districts across Bangladesh, including the capital city of Dhaka.
Weather reports indicate that strong winds could reach speeds of up to 60 kmph in the affected areas.
Residents in these regions are advised to stay cautious as the sudden onset of storms and lightning may cause disruptions.
The forecast warns of potential risks associated with high-velocity winds and heavy precipitation in these 20 districts.
